title: Rapid one-step CRISPR-cas vector assembly by isothermal spacer removal linearization and sequence-ligation independent cloning (ISRL-SLIC)☆☆☆
author: Madsen, Hanak, et al.
materials: To create a vector for direct cloning of protospacers in a binary Agrobacterium plasmid, BspQI recognition sites in pANIC_6A and pJG80 were deleted using site-directed mutagenesis. pANIC_6A was digested with BspQI, and the excised fragment was replaced by the amplicon of pANIC_delBspQI_Fw/Rv (Table 1) by In-Fusion® cloning. Clones were recovered on kanamycin selection. Likewise, pJG80 was digested with NheI and PstI. The excised fragment was replaced by the products of Cas9_NheI_Fw / Cas9_S_TCC_Rv and Cas9_S_TCC_Fw / Cas9_S_TCC_Rv (Table 1). Transformed E. coli (Stellar™) were selected using streptomycin. To assemble the vector, a Gateway reaction was performed according to the supplier’s manual (Invitrogen). The LR reaction contained pANIC_6a_ΔBspQI, pJG80_ΔBspQI and pJG85_BspQI_ccdB. The LR reaction was transformed into E. coli and recovered on LB-agar plates containing kanamycin and ampicillin. This strategy did not yield any correctly assembled clones after three attempts.

steps.title: Amplify ccdB cassette
steps.instruction: PCR‑amplify the ccdB cassette from pANIC_6A using primers ccdB_pJG85_Fw and ccdB_pJG85_Rv (Table 1).

steps.title: Linearize pJG85 with BsmBI
steps.instruction: Digest the pJG85 vector with BsmBI according to the manufacturer’s instructions to generate linearised backbone.

steps.title: In‑Fusion clone ccdB
steps.instruction: Combine the amplified ccdB fragment with BsmBI‑linearised pJG85 in an In‑Fusion® reaction following the kit protocol.

steps.title: Transform and select on chloramphenicol
steps.instruction: Transform the In‑Fusion reaction into competent E. coli, recover on LB‑agar plates containing chloramphenicol and incubate overnight.

steps.title: Amplify AmpR and ccdB for BspQI variant
steps.instruction: PCR‑amplify the ampicillin‑resistance cassette from pUC18 with primers AmpR_BspQI_Fw and AmpR_Rv, and the ccdB cassette from pANIC_6A with primers ccdBfusAmp_Fw and ccdB_pJG85_BspQI_Rv (Table 1).

steps.title: In‑Fusion clone AmpR and ccdB
steps.instruction: Insert both amplicons into prepared pJG85 (linearised as above) using In‑Fusion® cloning as described, then transform.

steps.title: Transform and select on ampicillin
steps.instruction: Plate transformed cells on LB‑agar containing ampicillin and incubate overnight; pick colonies for verification.

steps.title: Delete BspQI sites in pANIC_6A
steps.instruction: Digest pANIC_6A with BspQI, replace the excised fragment with the PCR product generated by primers pANIC_delBspQI_Fw/Rv (Table 1) using In‑Fusion® cloning; recover transformants on kanamycin plates.

steps.title: Delete BspQI sites in pJG80
steps.instruction: Digest pJG80 with NheI and PstI, replace the fragment with the combined PCR products of Cas9_NheI_Fw / Cas9_S_TCC_Rv and Cas9_S_TCC_Fw / Cas9_S_TCC_Rv (Table 1); transform Stellar™ E. coli and select on streptomycin plates.

steps.title: Perform Gateway LR assembly (failed)
steps.instruction: Set up a Gateway LR reaction containing pANIC_6a_ΔBspQI, pJG80_ΔBspQI and pJG85_BspQI_ccdB according to the Invitrogen manual, transform into E. coli and select on LB‑agar with kanamycin and ampicillin; note that no correct clones were obtained after three attempts.

steps.title: Create pANICΔRFP via In‑Fusion
steps.instruction: Digest pANIC_6A with SacI (11 539 bp fragment) and PstI (2 707 bp fragment); fuse these fragments with amplicons generated by primers pANICpatch_Fw/Rv, pANIC_NewMCS_Fw/Rv and a no‑template control using In‑Fusion® cloning to obtain pANICΔRFP, which now contains unique MluI, SacII and EcoRV sites in place of the RFP cassette.

steps.title: Remove BspQI from pANICΔRFP
steps.instruction: Delete the two BspQI sites from pANICΔRFP by the same site‑directed mutagenesis approach used for pANIC_6A, yielding pANICΔRFPΔBspQI.

steps.title: Digest pANICΔRFPΔBspQI and isolate fragment
steps.instruction: Digest pANICΔRFPΔBspQI with NcoI and SpeI, then gel‑purify the large resulting fragment.

steps.title: Digest pJG80ΔBspQI to excise Cas9
steps.instruction: Perform an EcoRI digest of pJG80ΔBspQI to release the Cas9 coding region.

steps.title: Amplify gRNA cassette with ccdB spacer
steps.instruction: PCR‑amplify the gRNA cassette containing the ccdB spacer from pJG85_BspQI_ccdB using primers TaU6_Fw_IF_EcoRICas and gRNA_Rv_IFSpeI.

steps.title: Amplify missing ZmUbi promoter part
steps.instruction: Amplify the missing segment of the ZmUbi promoter with primers ZmUbiNcoI_Fw and ZmUbiEcoRI_Rv from a previously Gateway‑assembled construct.

steps.title: Assemble pTRITIdirect vector
steps.instruction: Combine the NcoI‑SpeI fragment (from step 13), the EcoRI‑Cas9 fragment (step 14), the gRNA‑ccdB fragment (step 15) and the ZmUbi promoter fragment (step 16) by In‑Fusion® cloning to generate the final pTRITIdirect entry plasmid.

steps.title: Design model protospacer oligos
steps.instruction: Design 20 bp protospacer oligos containing XhoI, NotI and SacI sites; add a 17 bp overhang (ModelPS_Fw) and a 25 bp overhang (ModelPS_Rv) complementary to the termini of Esp3I/BsmBI‑linearised pJG85; ensure the overhangs have a calculated melting temperature > 50 °C. Design three additional model protospacers as listed in Table 1.

steps.title: Prepare protospacer dilution series
steps.instruction: Prepare independent dilution series for each protospacer from 1 nM to 10 µM (including 1 nM, 10 nM, 100 nM, 1 µM and 10 µM); the 1 nM dilution provides approximately a 1:1 molar ratio of plasmid to each oligo in the ISRL‑SLIC reaction.

steps.title: Single‑protospacer ISRL‑SLIC reaction
steps.instruction: Linearise pJG85 with Esp3I/BsmBI, mix with a single model protospacer oligo at the chosen concentration, and perform the ISRL‑SLIC reaction according to the protocol (isothermal incubation; exact time/temperature not specified).

steps.title: Multi‑protospacer ISRL‑SLIC reaction
steps.instruction: For two‑ or three‑protospacer assemblies, PCR‑amplify fragments containing TaU6, each protospacer and the gRNA scaffold; combine these fragments with the linearised target vector in an ISRL‑SLIC reaction under the same isothermal conditions.

steps.title: Transform and plate colonies
steps.instruction: Transform the ISRL‑SLIC reaction into competent E. coli, plate on LB‑agar containing the appropriate antibiotic (chloramphenicol for pJG85‑based reactions, kanamycin for pTRITIdirect), and incubate overnight.

steps.title: Count colonies and record efficiency
steps.instruction: Count colonies on each plate; note that 1 nM yields the fewest colonies, 10 µM yields the most for pJG85_BsmBI_ccdB, while the optimal range for pTRITIdirect is 10 nM–1 µM. Statistical significance was assessed (p ≤ 0.05 *, p ≤ 0.01 **, p ≤ 0.005 ***).

steps.title: Pick colonies for validation
steps.instruction: Select 30 colonies (six from each oligo concentration) for plasmid purification.

steps.title: Restriction‑digest validation of clones
steps.instruction: Digest each purified plasmid separately with NotI, SacI and XhoI; 22 of 30 clones show the expected pattern. Imperfect clones are distributed as two from 1 nM, two from 1 µM and four from 10 µM; no imperfect clones are observed at 10 nM and 100 nM.

steps.title: Sequence‑confirm selected clones
steps.instruction: Sequence all clones from the 1 nM and 10 µM sets and the two imperfect clones from the 1 µM set across the cloning site; all sequenced clones are correct, confirming high fidelity of the ISRL‑SLIC method.

steps.title: Test NEBuilder HiFi assembly (optional)
steps.instruction: Perform the ISRL‑SLIC cloning using the NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly kit in a single experiment; colonies were obtained, demonstrating that the method is independent of the In‑Fusion system.
